chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Aban, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abdillah, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about the egg-shaped helmet regarding which Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام cut off the hand, so he said: “It was an iron helmet that a man stole from the war booty, so he cut him.”

Because the proper understanding of this report is that the ruling is restricted to what Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام did, and there is nothing in the report stating that whoever steals from the war booty has his hand cut off such that it would contradict the first report. Rather, it is explicit in merely relating his action, and it is not impossible that Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام did that due to what the public interest at that moment required, especially since the first two reports explicitly state that there is no cutting off for him if he steals from the war booty. This is further supported by what he narrated: except when the value of what he stole exceeds what belongs to him by the value of a quarter dinar, for in that case as well cutting off becomes obligatory upon him. What he narrated indicates this detail:

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, whose action is being cited
key_terms.الْبَيْضَةِ: an iron helmet mentioned in the report as the stolen item
key_terms.الْمَصْلَحَةُ: the situational consideration or public interest mentioned in explaining the Imam's action
key_terms.الْمَغْنَمِ: war booty or spoils from which the theft occurred
key_terms.رُبُعِ دِينَارٍ: a quarter dinar, the threshold of excess value noted in the legal detail

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment apply to someone who steals from the war booty in Shi'a hadith?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal issue of theft from war booty and cites an incident in which Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام cut off the hand of a man who stole an iron helmet. The accompanying explanation clarifies that this action is not necessarily a general rule for all theft from war booty, and that the legal distinction depends on the thief's share and the excess value taken.
